gate1.walker_state: (sigma, Q) where sigma in {+1,-1}, Q in M_n(C)
gate1.reversal: Q -> U Q U^dagger, U ~ mu on U(n)
gate1.current: J = Tr(A @ q) for fixed coupling matrix A
gate1.verdict: The matrices enrich the internal state space but the observable algebra is classical. This is NOT a quantum substrate. It is a classical stochastic process with matrix-valued internal states.

trace_coupling.cp_note: CP always preserved because gamma(t) = sum S_k(1-exp(-r_k t))/r_k >= 0 when all S_k >= 0 and r_k > 0. This is the same CP guarantee as any positive-correlation Gaussian dephasing bath.
trace_coupling.markovianity_note: Non-Markovian (gamma(t) time-dependent) but this is the same type of non-Markovianity as any finite-memory bath. Not a new type of quantum dynamics.

gate4.verdict: The matrix PRW produces a constrained two-Lorentzian spectrum. A conventional two-bath model reproduces it exactly by choosing the rate ratio to match. The matrix PRW's constraint (ratio=2 for Haar) removes one parameter, but this is the same type of constrained relationship as the original fxt's P3 relation: a fixed ratio that is a special case of a more general conventional model. The constraint depends on the U distribution parameter p, which is itself a free input. DISTINCTIVE PREDICTION: NONE that survives conventional comparison.
